title: Green beans canned, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans cooked in butter or margarine are selected bean pods that are blanched, sterilized and sealed in a jar with butter. The product is ready to eat, has a mild buttery flavor and retains most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans are one of the most popular vegetables for canning because of their texture and taste.
In the United States the beans are traditionally cooked in butter, while some countries use margarine to reduce cost.
Canning allows storage for 2–3 years without loss of flavor.
Vitamin K levels in canned beans can be higher than in fresh beans due to the heat process.
Canned green beans are a common staple for camping and long trips as a vegetable source.

items.title: Good source of plant protein
items.content: Green beans provide about 2–3 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps you feel full.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Canned beans retain thiamine (B1), pyridoxine (B6) and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They contain iron, magnesium and potassium, which support heart and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Polysaccharides and flavonoids in beans help combat free radicals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking in butter raises the calorie count; those monitoring weight should consider this.

items.title: Bisphenol A
items.content: Some cans may be lined with epoxy resins; choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The beans are ready straight from the jar: add them to salads, soups, stews, or serve as a side dish. They can also be quickly warmed in a pan with extra herbs or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–4 days.
